definitions.explanation: An honorific term for someone's death, used to show respect for the deceased. Commonly used in formal announcements, obituaries, and news reporting about notable people.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}が{逝去|せいきょ}された。
{享年|きょうねん}{八十五|はちじゅうご}{歳|さい}で{逝去|せいきょ}されました。
examples.english: He passed away at the age of eighty-five.

examples.japanese: {著名|ちょめい}な{作家|さっか}の{逝去|せいきょ}を{悼|いた}み、{各地|かくち}で{追悼|ついとう}{式|しき}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: Memorial services were held across the country to mourn the passing of the renowned author.

notes:
USAGE NOTES:
{逝去|せいきょ} is an honorific (respectful) term for death. It elevates the deceased and should not be used when referring to one's own family members' deaths (use {亡|な}くなる instead) or in casual conversation.

FORMALITY:
This word belongs to formal/respectful register. In descending formality:
- {逝去|せいきょ} (honorific, for respected persons)
- {死去|しきょ} (neutral-formal, news reporting)
- {亡|な}くなる (standard polite)
- {死|し}ぬ (plain/blunt)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {逝去|せいきょ}される (to pass away — honorific form)
- {逝去|せいきょ}の{知|し}らせ (news of someone's passing)
- ご{逝去|せいきょ} (passing — with honorific prefix)

Often seen in the set phrase ご{逝去|せいきょ}を{悼|いた}み (mourning the passing of...).
